Subject: Recap + next steps: Private/VPC pricing and token volumes

Hi Alice — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can put together an accurate Private (VPC) quote for FintechCo: 

1) Usage profile: you mentioned two main workloads — real-time chat (low-latency, ~60% of calls) and overnight batch embedding + summarization for compliance (40%). Please confirm approximate monthly token volumes for each workload. If you don't have exact numbers, a range is fine (e.g., 50M–150M tokens/month chat, 200M–400M tokens/month batch).

2) Deployment & environments: you said you'll need a production VPC and a staging VPC (separate networks). Confirm number of environments and whether QA will be shared with staging or needs a third environment.

3) Licensing model preference: we can offer a capacity-based Dedicated-like commit for Private (monthly reserved GPUs + perpetual licensing) or a SaaS-style usage billing with a platform license. Do you have a preference or procurement constraints?

4) Support tier & SLAs: do you need enterprise 24x7 on-call and accelerated incident response, or will standard business-hours support suffice for now?

5) Budget & unit economics: we typically anchor conversations around target unit price per 1M tokens for cost modeling. Do you have a target $/1M tokens or an internal budget range we should hit?

Attachments: I'm including a stub SOC2 snapshot and a draft SOW outline to speed procurement review.

Next steps: if you can reply with the volumes + env count + budget range, I'll produce a tailored quote and matrix that shows licensing vs consumption pricing and recommended support tiers.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Ben — thanks for the clear recap. See answers below (rough numbers for now while I pull exact telemetry):

1) Volumes (monthly, approximate):
- Real-time chat: 120M tokens/month
- Batch embedding + summarization: 350M tokens/month
Total: ~470M tokens/month

2) Environments: production (separate VPC), staging (separate VPC). QA will be a shared slice of staging for now — so 2 environments total. We may add a dedicated compliance environment later.

3) Licensing preference: Procurement prefers a fixed-cost licensing model for budgeting (monthly platform + support + per-token overage). Open to a reserved-capacity commit if the numbers are compelling.

4) Support tier: for initial deployment, business-hours with 8x5 coverage is acceptable. We may upgrade to 24x7 once in production if latency issues occur.

5) Budget: the finance team has given a preliminary target of $8,000–$12,000/month for platform + support, excluding cloud infra. For unit economics, they're thinking in terms of $20–$30 per 1M tokens as a target for vendor/platform cost (not including downstream infra).

Let me know if you need anything else — I'll try to pull exact telemetry and a higher-fidelity breakdown by API call type.

Thanks,
Alice
Head of ML Platforms, FintechCo
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: Private/VPC pricing and token volumes

Great — this is exactly what we needed, thanks. A few notes and initial pricing directions based on your ranges: 

- Volume: 470M tokens/mo maps to ~5.64B tokens/year. For Private/VPC we'd model both a licensing (platform subscription + support) and a reserve-capacity commit that includes a baseline GPU pool.

- Unit economics: your target of $20–$30 / 1M tokens is helpful. To be transparent, in a Private deployment with reserved capacity we can show effective platform+inference unit costs in the $12–$22 / 1M tokens range depending on model family, quantization, and KV-cache effectiveness. SaaS-style (pure usage billing) typically runs a bit higher, ~$25–$40 / 1M tokens at these volumes.

- Environments: for 2 VPCs we'd include separate environment licensing lines; a small discount applies for multi-env bundles. If you later add a dedicated compliance env we'll convert to a 3-env bundle.

- Support: we'll price Standard (8x5) support in the base SOW; I'll include an optional upgrade line for 24x7 Enterprise support with faster SLAs.

Next steps: I'll put together a two-row quote: (A) Platform subscription + Standard support + reserved capacity (monthly) with per-month amortized token unit cost and (B) Usage billing model with platform fee + per-token. I'll include assumptions (model family, typical prompt/response lengths, cache hit rates). Expect the draft SOW and quote by EOD tomorrow.

FYI Marissa — looping you in to align on licensing + SOW language; I'll need a short SOW + licensing template for Private deals.

-Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Alice Zhang <alice@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-11-17 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: Private/VPC pricing and token volumes

Hi Alice — nice to meet you digitally. A couple of procurement/contract notes up front: 

- Licensing: our Private licensing for VPC has two common options: a) Subscription model (monthly platform fee + per-environment license) or b) Reserved capacity commit (monthly GPU pool charge + platform license). Both include the same console/observability features; reserved capacity just gives a stronger throughput SLA and lower per-token effective cost.

- Support: Standard (included) is 8x5 with 24-hour response for Sev1 and 72-hour for Sev3. Enterprise 24x7 includes guaranteed 1-hour response for Sev1 and a named technical account manager. We'll put both as line items in the SOW.

- Compliance & onboarding: for SOC2 evidence we can provide a snapshot (attached) and a short-run onboarding plan. For a compliance environment we recommend a dedicated network/segregated KV encryption keys.

We'll draft SOW language that reflects the two pricing paths Ben mentioned and include a simple cost comparison table anchored to your $20–$30 / 1M token target. Ben — please share the model/quantization assumptions you plan to use so I can populate the cost scenarios.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Enterprise Sales Ops
